findings.reason: without resolving it the plan instructs a rebuild of work already on main, which is the same defect two earlier reviews had answered for §49, §51 and §44.
findings.text: f-wftl-019 is open and recommends `/reckon-build work-flows-to-the-lane §22`, while the same document declares s22 done and records its landing at `0ce618ed84` in c-close-s22, so a coordinator driving the plan from its open followups dispatches a landed section again

findings.reason: the deliverable's second promise would go unmeasured, and the gate would report that promise held on the strength of a case that never distinguished fixed from unfixed.
findings.text: §64's second case ("times a presence lookup for a missing run against a current index, and reads it under one second with no write transaction opened") is already true at the base revision, because `_ensure` returns as soon as `current()` holds and `has_row` then runs only SELECTs, so the case passes on the unfixed code and measures nothing

findings.reason: the fixture as written can pass without exercising the repeated-rebuild mechanism the section exists to remove, so the node's whole measure would rest on a case that cannot fail.
findings.text: §64's first case ("one station tick over 50 fixture terminal runs and counts at most one rebuild") does not state what makes the index stale during the tick or that any lookup misses the run-file fast path, and `has_row` answers from the run file when it exists while a fixture with no ledger write in it rebuilds once even on the base code, so the count is one either way

findings.reason: a second case naming a reason and reading it recorded on the pointer makes the record's second half checkable, and without it the plan accepts the same silent loss of a stated reason that §61 refuses for a named backend.
findings.text: §63's Deliverable promises the over-fence note carries "the reason if one is given", but its Done when tests only the no-reason dispatch and batch-queue, so an implementation that accepts `--over-fence REASON` and discards the reason passes the gate
